criteria: A versioned evidence schema, reproducible build instructions and at least 12 labelled positive and negative cases are published and checked by the independent technical reviewer.
A public test suite with CI results shows that missing, changed or unsupported evidence cannot produce a verified match.
milestones.name: Reproducible evidence contract

criteria: An Ethereum mainnet transaction-path matcher for the documented call and proxy types is published, with reproducible passing results on a frozen public test set.
Reviewed-commit and live-code comparisons are published, with every unsupported or unresolved case named and checked by the technical reviewer.
milestones.name: Runtime and audit-scope matching

criteria: A working MetaMask demonstration and an agent rules adapter are published, with public tests for changed code, missing evidence and attempts to bypass the rules.
An independent security assessment of the integration and evidence checks is published, with fixes rechecked.
milestones.name: Wallet and agent integration

criteria: At least 5 unaffiliated wallet or agent-execution teams use the evidence check in live Ethereum mainnet workflows for at least 30 days, verified by the technical reviewer.
At least 1 of them must be: MetaMask, Rabby, Trust Wallet, Ledger, Safe, Coinbase Wallet, Rainbow, Phantom, Trezor or Ambire, confirmed by that team or the technical reviewer.
Published adoption evidence excludes founder-run demonstrations, test accounts and unused installs.
A business plan for covering ongoing maintenance and at least $500 of revenue earned from paid integrations.
milestones.name: Independent wallet and agent adoption

sections.commitments:
- Code funded by this grant is released under Apache-2.0 and evidence data under CC BY 4.0.
- Proof Before Sign stays free for wallet users. Published evidence stays free to read.
- Paid integrations for AI APIs, agents and other high-volume services are planned to cover hosting after the grant. Exact rates are in each customer's commercial terms and can be shared with the technical reviewer.
- Proof of Audits maintains the released components and ships security fixes for 12 months after the final milestone.
- Every result is one of MATCHED, CHANGED, PARTIAL or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN is never treated as approval.
- Payment never changes what the evidence says.
sections.in_scope:
- Reproduce the proposed transaction at a pinned Ethereum mainnet state, naming the external calls, proxy implementations and dependencies it reaches.
- Match the code that runs to the reviewed source revision with reproducible compiler inputs and bytecode comparison.
- Attach the audit report, reviewed commit, scope, relevant findings and fix rechecks to each claim.
- Flag changed implementations, unresolved calls, code outside any audit scope and who holds upgrade rights, without producing false matches.
- A wallet evidence panel and a versioned integration API.
- An agent adapter that enforces the wallet owner's own approval rules. An AI model cannot override them.
- Published evidence fixtures, test results, known limits and integration documentation.
sections.out_scope:
- Audit contests or researcher payments, which are a separate initiative.
- Auditor bonds, slashing or loss compensation.
- Any claim that an audited transaction is safe.
- Chains other than Ethereum mainnet.
- A promise that a simulated transaction will run the same way once included onchain.
sections.team:
I'm M K Veerendra Vamshi, founder of Proof of Audits and a smart-contract security researcher. I placed first in Sherlock's Allbridge Core Yield audit contest in 2025.

I started Proof of Audits to solve a problem I kept seeing in Web3 security: teams spend heavily on audits, but users still cannot tell whether the contracts they're interacting with are the code that was reviewed.

We've built a working transaction-analysis service, a MetaMask Snap and a public Ethereum evidence explorer. We've also started onboarding auditors to the platform, so we're building both the technology and the researcher network behind it.

At Devcon and DSS Mumbai, I connected with people from Sigma Prime, ChainSecurity, corpus.core and other Ethereum security teams. These conversations opened opportunities to explore integrations, share audit evidence and work together. They are relationships we're developing, not partnerships we're claiming are already signed.

I lead the product, security research and engineering. The grant will allow us to bring in specialist engineering and independent security review capacity, while I remain responsible for delivery and adoption.

https://proofofaudits.com
sections.why:
An audit tells you which code was reviewed. Your wallet asks you to approve a transaction using the code deployed today, and it doesn't tell you whether they're the same.

We analysed 12 Ethereum transactions involving 97 contract calls (https://proofofaudits.com/demos/proof-before-sign). Only 2 calls had a recorded byte-for-byte match to a reviewed build. Another 74 ran code in files named in audit reports, and 21 had no matching public audit in our records.

Those are very different levels of evidence, and none of that difference is visible when someone presses Confirm.

Proof Before Sign brings that evidence into the wallet. Before the user signs, it shows what matches reviewed code, what has changed and what remains unverified. AI agents can also be required to follow the owner's evidence rules.

A matching audit is not a guarantee of safety, but users should at least know what they are relying on.
sections.why_grant:
We've already done the work needed to show this problem can be solved. Now we need to make the solution reliable enough for other teams to use, and get it into the wallets where it matters.

Our live analyzer has checked 12 real Ethereum transactions involving 97 contract calls. Only 2 had recorded byte-for-byte matches to reviewed code. Another 74 were linked to audit scope, while 21 had no matching public audit evidence.

We've also built an explorer covering 656 functions across ten major Ethereum protocols, reproduced deployed Aave V4 and Uniswap V2 code from reviewed commits, and developed a MetaMask Snap that displays this evidence before signing. The code is public, although the independent evidence release process and ordinary MetaMask distribution are not complete.

We're not starting from zero on distribution either. Auditors have already joined our platform, we have an API for audit firms to publish their evidence, and Devcon gave us direct connections with security researchers, audit firms and Ethereum infrastructure teams interested in exploring the product.

**The next challenge is getting this into everyday use.**

The grant will fund three things:

- **Finish the product:** Complete the difficult execution-path checks, strengthen evidence verification, commission independent security reviews and prepare the wallet and agent integrations for production use.
- **Bring in the evidence:** Work with auditors, audit firms and protocols to connect reviewed source code, findings and fixes to the contracts running on Ethereum.
- **Get it into wallets:** Turn our Devcon connections into technical pilots, give external wallet and agent teams integration support, and prove that they use the checks in real Ethereum workflows.

We already have the product foundation and the relationships to begin this work. A new team would need to build that foundation before attempting the same integrations.

The final $25,000 of this grant is tied to adoption: at least two independent wallet or agent teams must use the evidence checks in live Ethereum workflows for 30 days, including at least one established provider. An independent reviewer will verify that use.

We're not asking TheDAO to fund another audit dashboard. We're asking it to help put existing audit evidence in front of people at the moment they are about to trust a contract with their funds.

**Existing work:**

https://proofofaudits.com/demos/proof-before-sign

https://proofofaudits.com/explorer/functions

https://github.com/ProofOfAudits/proof-before-sign-snap

initiative.summary: Wallets ask users to approve transactions without showing whether the code they will run is the code that was audited. Proof Before Sign shows, inside the wallet and before signing, which calls in a transaction match reviewed code, which are only inside an audit's scope, and which have no matching public audit evidence. AI agents that sign for their owners can be held to the same evidence rules.
initiative.title: Proof of Audits: Proof Before Sign for Ethereum Wallets and Agents
